# PR #3664: Patch: an Anomaly's cast holds the phone frame budget on the living board under 4x throttling

Closes #3633

This is the first pass on #3633, landed as @MaxGoetzmann chose (option 1). The living-board spec, `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx`, **still fails** (1/4 locally) and will stay red in the daily super run until the follow-up below lands. That follow-up issue isn't open yet: I have no GitHub access, so **a person needs to open it** with the text at the end of this description.

## What changed and why

The earlier passes profiled the living board in Chrome at 4x CPU throttling. The frames were going to whole-board style recalculations, slow board relayouts and full re-renders of the board on every queue step. The changes, all in `apps/web` plus one e2e spec:

- **`:has()` rules replaced by attributes.**
  - The 11 `.app-shell--wide:has(> .game) …` rules in `board.css` now key off `[data-game-host]`. `Game` sets it on its parent while it is mounted (`GAME_HOST_ATTRIBUTE`). A `:has()` followed by `> *` made Blink restyle the whole document on every effect.
  - The changing `.game:has(…)` rules now read marks on the game root instead:
    - `Game` sets `data-card-played`, `data-drag` and `data-game-over`.
    - `FxLayer` sets `data-fx-layer`, `data-fx-banner` and `data-fx-hold`.
    - `Prompt` sets its cell's mark.
    - Specificity is kept by doubling the attribute.
  - A new guard, `hasSelectors.test.ts`, fails on any new rule of either kind.
- **Custom properties written where they are read.** The entry's timing variables (`--slam-land-ms` and the rest) are written onto the elements that read them (`game/rootVars.ts`) instead of onto the game root, where each change restyled the whole game. They are registered with `@property … inherits: false`. A guard test, `rootVars.test.ts`, holds this.
- **Phone field relayout.** The phone `.field` now states its lanes' minimum height (`--lane-row-min`, `--lanes-min`) instead of leaving Blink to compute it. Computing it laid the lanes out twice on every relayout, restyling every size-container zone's card both times. `arena.css` sets `--lane-row-min` instead of its own lane rows.
- **Fewer re-renders per queue step.**
  - `Card` is memoized with a comparator, `sameCardProps`: of the `animating` map it compares only the keys that card reads, and it compares inline data by value. `CardFace`, `MinionFace` and `Log` are memoized too.
  - `useIsHeld(relevant)`: a card that can't tilt or open full screen no longer re-renders when the queue starts or stops.
  - The highlight object, the keyword-loss set and the click handlers stay stable between steps.
  - Before, a queue step re-rendered the whole board (about 540 components) twice; now it re-renders a few dozen.
- **Director reads before it writes.** In `director.ts`, each frame measures the boxes of all its due effect cues before it mounts any of them. A stage cue still runs in its place in the order, because a hold, pull or lunge moves what later cues measure.
- **Spec (`fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx`).**
  - The pass/fail check now runs after `layout:report`, so the last attempt's row is in the log even when it fails (the issue's optional item).
  - The Mythic takeover plays a fresh card on each attempt. Replaying the same card's events over the reset board played no takeover.

### This pass

- **Merge conflict in `Game.tsx` resolved.** Main's hovered-attack preview (`hovered` passed to `withOutcomes`, `useAimEmitter` moved up) is kept alongside this branch's kept highlight. `sameHighlight` now also compares `outcomes` and `hoveredAttack`; without that, moving the pointer to another target under the same outcomes would have kept the old preview.
- **New test:** `#3633 sameHighlight keeps a highlight that lights the same things and drops one that does not`. I checked that it fails when the `hoveredAttack` comparison is removed.
- **New fragment:** `crates/cards/patches/pending/an-anomaly-s-cast-holds-the-phone-frame-budget-on-the-living.json`, marked `visual` and with a player line under `fixes`. `CardFace.tsx`, `MinionFace.tsx` and `tilt.ts` are under `apps/web/src/cards/`, so the classifier counts this as a change to how cards look, and R2529000 asks for a claiming fragment.

## How it measures now

Local run of `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` on the merged tree, Chrome at 4x throttling. Each cell is mean / worst frame in ms; the budget is 50 / 120. CI had logged 173–963 ms mean for the cast before.

| Size | Anomaly cast, attempts 1 / 2 / 3 | Mythic takeover, attempts 1 / 2 / 3 |

The forced-shed test passes. Each size test stops at its first failing moment, so the Starship launch and the later moments were not reached in this run.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `vitest run` on `Game`, `attackOutcome`, `Card.memo`, `Card`, `hasSelectors`, `rootVars` tests | 107/107 pass |
| harness command: `vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …` | 10,137 pass, 3 timed out at 5 s while a cargo build ran alongside |

- **No required CI check has run on this head yet.**

## Decisions the issue didn't settle

- **Field minimum instead of explicit lane rows.** The plan's explicit lane-row formulas (`max(var(--card-h), …)`) gave no gain. Setting the field's `min-height: 0` alone moved boxes at 320x480. The stated minimum (`content-box`, the four row floors plus three gaps) kept every zone box identical (≤0.01 px) at 11 sizes across 3 boards.
- **Stage cues stay where they fall in the director's order.** The plan said to move them first; that would change what later cues in the same frame measure.
- **Highlight kept by value, not memo deps alone.** A new view whose moves arrive later rebuilds an identical highlight; keeping the old object stops every card re-rendering.
- **Attribute marks instead of a narrower `:has()`.** A `:where(.game ~ *, :has(~ .game))` rewrite measured 162–169 ms mean, against about 95–120 ms with the attribute.
- **A `visual` fragment despite no visible change.** Main's three pending `visual` fragments would let `--claims` pass for now. Without our own, the check would start failing once those ship ahead of this PR. #3613's follow-up was claimed the same way.
- **Not done:** raising the budget, lowering the throttle, the shed at 844x390 (that would need a new ruling), or cutting any layer, beat or timing.

## Worth a second look

- `sameCardProps` in `Card.tsx`: any prop it doesn't list still forces a re-render, so a new prop costs speed, never correctness.
- `rootVars.ts`: one `<style>` per variable, written in an insertion effect.
- `Game.tsx`'s host cleanup: it removes the attribute only if no other `.game` child remains, because React runs the cleanup before detaching the element.

**Title:** `Patch: the living board's standing scene holds the phone frame budget: card art, backs and portrait motes animate on composited layers`

The current rows are in the table above.

**Proposal.**
- Animate the moving faces' art, the backs' breathing and the portrait motes on composited HTML layers (transform and opacity on their own elements) instead of SVG groups and filters, so a frame restyles none of them.
- Let the phone director shed within a moment, not only between them.
- Stay inside R3351000 and R2803000: no raised budget, no lower throttle, no cut layer, beat, hold or timing.

**Acceptance.**

- The `layout:report` rows show every moment within 50 ms mean and 120 ms worst at all three sizes, in at least one of `FRAME_ATTEMPTS` plays.

# #3633: Patch: an Anomaly's cast holds the phone frame budget on the living board under 4x throttling
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

R3351000 (#3351, built in #3467) says the living game holds the shared phone budget at 390x844, 360x780 and 844x390 under 4x CPU throttling: a mean frame within `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` (50 ms) and a worst frame within `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` (120 ms). Its living board has five art-first Units with tile auras, an Anomaly's backdrop, a launched Starship and a hand of ten, one card tilted. On a throttled phone that board does not hold it. When an Anomaly's cast plays over it, each frame takes hundreds of milliseconds. This is the last red job in the daily super run on `staging`, so production can't promote itself until it is fixed.

### Why

`e2e/cypress/component/fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` has never got this far in CI until now.
- Its first run, the daily super run [42664754927](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42664754927), failed earlier, on its tile-aura count. #3437 had given three of its five Units their own tile auras 77 minutes after #3467 merged, and an own aura replaces the default tile aura.
- #3530 fixes that count. The size tests then reach the budget, and fail on their first moment, "Anomaly cast", at all three sizes.
- #3530 also makes a starved sample window one more replayed window (`FRAME_ATTEMPTS` = 3), and prints every sample through `layout:report`.

In [run 42745204160](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42745204160/job/129601569615) (ci.yml dispatched with `e2e: all` on `bcfc7155bc`), the logged samples were:

```

390x844  attempt 2: mean frame 270.4ms over 8 frames  [min=60 p50=320 p90=525 max=525]   worst 525ms

360x780  attempt 2: mean frame 450.2ms over 6 frames  [min=166 p50=257 p90=1116 max=1116] worst 1116ms
844x390  attempt 1: mean frame 173.4ms over 13 frames [min=47 p50=179 p90=216 max=451]   worst 451ms

So every window misses the 50 ms mean by 3.5 to 19 times, and the 120 ms worst by 3.5 to 12 times. These aren't one-time costs: the second play, with the backdrop already decoded, is as slow. Some comparisons:
- `fx-phone-frame.cy.tsx`'s "R3337003 an Anomaly's cast holds the phone frame budget mid-flight" passes, but on a lighter board and without throttling.
- The living game's fourth test, "a forced shed sheds motes first and a set piece's beats never", passes.

### Proposal

Root-cause where the frames go: profile the living board's Anomaly cast in Chrome under 4x throttling at 390x844. Suspects, none confirmed:
- the canvas motes of six tile auras plus the Anomaly's particles;
- the backdrop's layers;
- the moving faces' CSS animations under the rift;
- the tilted card's pointer loop;
- a layout or style recalculation per frame from the set piece's DOM (`[data-fx="rift"]`).

Then fix the product so the shed (R3351000: motes first, then far auras, then faces) or the scene's own cost brings the frames within budget.

R3351000 and R2803000 rejected raising the budget, and the 4x throttle is the ruling's own condition. Change either only with a person's ruling, and never by loosening the spec.

### Acceptance

- `e2e component (chrome)` passes `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` 4/4: in the daily super run, or with `ci.yml` dispatched with `e2e: all` on the branch, since a pull request's CI does not run component specs.

`apps/web/src/fx/` (the aura and mote layers, the shed and the Anomaly set piece) and `apps/web/src/game/`. The spec only if the profile shows it measures something other than the board.
